subject: science
passage: Home bakers often say that bread dough rises faster in a ceramic bowl than in a metal one. Some bakers even warm their ceramic bowls before putting the dough in. Food scientist Mikael Virtanen hypothesizes that the difference comes down to temperature: ceramic holds warmth better than metal, so dough in a ceramic bowl stays warmer, and yeast produces gas more quickly in warm dough.
stem: Which finding, if true, would most directly weaken Virtanen's hypothesis?

choices.A: Dough in ceramic bowls stayed a few degrees warmer than dough in metal bowls as it rose.
choices.B: Dough still rose faster in ceramic than in metal when both were held at the same temperature.
choices.C: Yeast produces gas much more slowly in dough that has been kept in a refrigerator.
choices.D: Bakers who use metal bowls often cover them with a damp cloth to keep the dough from drying out.

explanation.why: Virtanen claims that warmth is the reason dough rises faster in ceramic bowls. If the ceramic bowls still win when temperature is the same in both, the difference must come from something other than temperature.
explanation.A: Incorrect. Dough staying warmer in ceramic is exactly what Virtanen's explanation needs, so this supports it.
explanation.B: Correct. With temperature held equal, ceramic still made dough rise faster, so temperature cannot explain the difference.
explanation.C: Incorrect. This only repeats the general point that cold slows yeast; it does not test whether temperature explains the difference between the bowls.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Covering bowls with a cloth does not show why one kind of bowl makes dough rise faster than the other.
